title: Cross-Team Rotation & Stretch Assignment Playbook
author: Mariana Soto
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines Redwood's formal Cross-Team Rotation & Stretch Assignment program (the Program). The Program helps ICs and managers coordinate short-term, low-risk rotations and stretch assignments that accelerate skill growth, increase cross-functional knowledge, and surface future leaders. This is a standardized, auditable alternative to ad-hoc rotations.

Scope and goals
- Scope: All full‑time and fixed‑term employees with 6+ months tenure are eligible unless otherwise restricted by compliance, export-control, or customer commitments.
- Goals:
  - Fast-path cross-functional learning while minimizing product/regulatory risk.
  - Provide measurable skill transfer and career signal for promotions/role changes.
  - Reduce hiring needs by filling short-term capability gaps internally.

Program types (examples)
1) Rotation (temporary reassignment)
   - Duration: 8–24 weeks (typical: 12 weeks)
   - Ownership: Host team manager holds day-to-day supervision; home manager retains performance review responsibility unless formally transferred.
2) Stretch assignment (project-based contribution)
   - Duration: 4–12 weeks (typical: 6–8 weeks)
   - Ownership: Home manager remains primary; assignment lead sets deliverables and success criteria.
3) Shadowing (observational, onboarding adjacent)
   - Duration: 2–6 weeks

Eligibility matrix (summary)
| Eligibility factor | Rotation | Stretch | Shadowing |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Tenure >= 6 months | Required | Preferred | Optional |
| Manager approval (home) | Required | Required | Recommended |
| Host team capacity | Required | Required | Optional |
| Security/customer constraints | Review required | Review required | Usually allowed |

How the program works (process)

1) Candidate initiation
   - Employee/manager submits a "Rotation Request" via People Portal (GrowthPath > Programs > Rotation Request) with: motivation, target skills, proposed duration, and proposed start date. Attach a 1‑page project brief for stretch assignments.
2) Home manager review (within 3 business days)
   - Approve/decline. If approved, manager adds proposed success criteria and confirms coverage plan for the employee's responsibilities.
3) Host manager review (within 5 business days)
   - Evaluate workload, propose onboarding plan and mentor, confirm capacity, and agree on success criteria and exposure limits (e.g., production access).
4) People Ops approval & compliance check (within 5 business days)
   - Validate total headcount impact, compensation/conflict checks, and any customer/contractual constraints. For Private/Enterprise-customer-facing roles require Security signoff.
5) Finalize assignment and kickoff
   - Sign a one-page "Rotation Agreement" in People Portal. Kickoff meeting within 3 business days involving home manager, host manager, employee, and assigned mentor.

Manager responsibilities
- Home manager:
  - Ensure workload coverage and document temporary delegation in a JIRA board (project: CAREER-ROTATIONS, label: coverage).
  - Maintain primary performance and promotion ownership unless an explicit transfer is completed.
  - Conduct mid-rotation check-in at 50% duration.
- Host manager:
  - Provide a concrete onboarding checklist, mentor (named), and weekly syncs.
  - Assign clear deliverables tied to learning outcomes.
  - Limit production risk by scoping write access and pairing the rotator with an experienced engineer for the first 2 weeks.

People Ops & Program Admin responsibilities
- Program Admin (People Ops) maintains program calendar, quarterly slot capacity, and a public rotations dashboard.
- Track participation metrics: rotations started, completion rate, promotion signal, average duration, NPS (post-rotation), and manager feedback. Target: 80% completion, median NPS >= 4.0.

Tooling & templates (where to act)
- People Portal (GrowthPath > Programs): submit/approve requests and store Rotation Agreements.
- JIRA: CAREER-ROTATIONS project — tracking tickets for coverage, onboarding, and deliverables. Use labels: rotation-id, host-team, home-team.
- Slack: #rotations-announcements (read-only), #rotation-support (people-ops support). Use /rotations-status to fetch an employee's active rotation via the HR Bot.
- Confluence: Use the follow-up "Rotation Report" template (located: /confluence/company-handbook/rotation-templates) to capture outcomes.

Onboarding & safety controls
- Access policy: default to read-only access for host-team production systems for first 2 weeks. Elevated access requires host manager + security endorsement + People Ops logging.
- Data handling: If rotation touches customer data, the rotator must complete the "Customer Data & Access" class and sign the temporary access addendum.
- Escalation: If the host manager identifies a compliance or incident risk, pause the rotation immediately and inform People Ops and Security (incident@redwood.example).

Success criteria & evaluation
- Predefined success criteria are required for all rotations and stretch assignments. Examples include:
  - Deliverable completion (project milestone shipped)
  - Skills checklist (skill X: intermediate -> advanced)
  - Mentor signoff on pairing sessions (minimum 8 sessions)
- Post-rotation report (due 7 days after end): Employee writes a 1-page summary, host manager provides feedback, and home manager recommends next steps (return, extend, transfer).
- Impact signals used in promotions: skills acquired, cross-team impact, sustained performance on home job after return, and mentor/host feedback.

Capacity planning & quotas
- Teams may have a maximum of 10% of FTEs on active rotations at a time unless approved by the manager's director. For small teams (<10 people) cap is 1 active rotator.
- People Ops publishes quarterly capacity by team on the program dashboard. To request a quota exception, create a CAREER-ROTATIONS JIRA ticket and get Director approval.

Compensation and title implications
- Compensation remains under the home team while on rotation. Any title or band changes require a formal role transfer and compensation review submitted at least 4 weeks before the desired effective date.

Edge cases and FAQ
- Long-running customer commitments: Rotations are limited if the employee is on an active critical customer escalation. People Ops and the host manager will coordinate a phased partial-time rotation if the customer approval allows.
- Extension requests: Can be submitted via People Portal; require home + host manager signoff and People Ops approval 2 weeks before planned end date.

Reporting and program KPIs (quarterly)
- Participation rate (unique participants / total FTE)
- Completion rate (target: >= 80%)
- Promotion conversion within 12 months of rotation (target: 10% lift vs baseline)
- Rotation NPS (target: >= 4.0)
- Time-to-productivity for rotators in host teams (target: median 2 weeks to first meaningful PR)

Templates & artifacts (quick links)
- Rotation Request form: People Portal > Programs > Rotation Request
- Rotation Agreement (one page): People Portal > Programs > Templates
- Post-rotation Report template: Confluence > rotation-templates > post-rotation-report
- Manager checklist: Confluence > rotation-templates > manager-checklist

Governance and exceptions
- Quarterly program review: People Ops + Manager Council review capacity, outcomes, and policy adjustments.
- Exception policy: Director-level signoff for any rotation > 24 weeks or involving transfer of compensation/title mid-rotation.

Appendix: Sample Rotation Agreement (one-page)
- Employee: name, role, home team
- Host team: name, manager, mentor
- Dates: start / end / working hours and location
- Scope: top 3 objectives and success criteria
- Access limits: list of systems and data access rules
- Coverage plan: how home work will be handled
- Signatures: home manager, host manager, employee, People Ops

Frequently used internal IDs & commands
- JIRA project: CAREER-ROTATIONS
- Slack channels: #rotation-support, #rotations-announcements
- Confluence template hub: /confluence/company-handbook/rotation-templates
- HR Bot commands: `/rotations-status @username`, `/rotation-request start`
